plan.title: What you have plenty of, and what you lack

intake.question: How long has this been going on?

options.label: On and off for over a year

intake.question: What do you want from it?

strong.text:
Your chart is the strong kind, {dm_short}, and that adds a twist to why you stay. Strong charts don't usually stay out of fear. They stay because they assume they're in charge of it. You can leave whenever you want, so there's no rush, so you don't. Meanwhile months go by. Ask yourself a blunt question: if you're the one in control, why hasn't anything been decided? Sometimes the answer is that you like the option more than the person. Sometimes it's that you're waiting for them to step up so you don't have to ask. Either way, being able to leave at any moment is not the same as choosing to stay. Make it a choice.

A practical way to make it a choice: give the current setup a review date, the way you'd review anything else you've invested in. Put it in your calendar a month from now. On that day, answer three questions on paper. Am I getting what I want? Have I asked for it? Did anything change after I asked? If all three answers are no, the review is over and so is the arrangement.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can leave any time, so you never do. Cute. Pick on purpose.

weak.text:
Your chart is the weak kind, {dm_short}, and that colors why you stay. A weak chart tends to treat any warmth as something it should be grateful for. A good night, a sweet text, an invite out of nowhere, and you feel lucky, so you don't ask for more in case asking breaks it. That makes an undefined thing feel safer than it is. Here's a test. Imagine a friend describing your exact setup to you, with the same texts, the same gaps, the same weekends. Would you tell them they're lucky, or would you tell them they deserve to know where they stand? Give yourself the same advice you'd give them.

It also helps to notice the moments when you feel most grateful to them. Gratitude is lovely, but in an undefined relationship it can work like a sedative. You feel lucky after a good night, so you stop asking questions for another two weeks. Next time you feel that rush, enjoy it, and then ask yourself one quiet question the morning after: was that a good night, or a good relationship?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: What would you tell a friend in your exact spot? Say that to yourself.

rat.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. It shows how you are up close, in the room where a partner would live. Yours is the Rat, 子, deep Water and one of the four peach-blossom branches, the ones classical readers link with charm. You attract easily, often at night, often through conversation. In a situationship that means interest is rarely the problem. Depth is. The Rat keeps its best thoughts in reserve and tests the ground before it trusts it, so you may be giving them the witty version of you and keeping the real one in the burrow. If you want more than a fun maybe, let them see one thing you usually keep back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat in your spouse palace. Charming at midnight, guarded at noon. Show the noon version.

ox.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. It shows how you are in close partnership. Yours is the Ox, 丑, wet winter Earth that stores Metal and Water inside it. The Ox is patient, loyal and slow to commit, and once it commits it stays. That's why a situationship can suit you longer than it should: you're willing to wait, and you assume steady effort will eventually be recognized. Sometimes it is. Sometimes the other person is simply enjoying your reliability for free. The Ox's lesson here is that patience needs a deadline, or it turns into a field nobody plants.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox spouse palace: loyal and patient. Give the patience a deadline.

tiger.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace, the private room where a partner lives. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire hidden in it, and one of the travel branches classical readers call yeokma, the moving horse. You need motion in love: new places, new plans, a partner who keeps up. An undefined thing can feel like freedom to a Tiger, right up until it starts to feel like a cage you never agreed to. Then you leave fast. If this one matters, say so before the restlessness decides for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger spouse palace. You love the chase, then bolt. Say something before you bolt.

rabbit.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure Wood and one of the four peach-blossom branches, linked with charm, taste and an easy social glow. People like being around you, which means you rarely lack options and often lack clarity. A Rabbit spouse palace wants gentleness and beauty in love, and avoids conflict to protect them. In a situationship you might keep things pleasant rather than true. Pleasant is lovely. It's just not the same as known. One honest, slightly awkward question will do more for you than another perfect evening.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit spouse palace: everything stays pleasant. Ask one slightly awkward question.

dragon.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth that stores Water, and one of the four storehouse branches. Storehouses keep a lot inside. You may have big private hopes about this person that you've never said out loud, because a Dragon imagines whole futures quietly. It also has pride and can wait for the other person to prove themselves first. The trouble with an inner storehouse is that nobody else can see what's in it. Open the door a little. Tell them one piece of the future you've been imagining.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon spouse palace: a whole secret future in storage. Share one room of it.

snake.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal hidden inside, and one of the travel branches. The Snake is perceptive, private and strategic in love. You notice everything they do and reveal very little of what you think about it. That makes you magnetic and hard to read, which keeps a situationship going in a fog. You may already know more about where this stands than they do. Use that knowledge honestly: say what you've noticed, kindly, and ask about it directly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake spouse palace: you notice everything. Say one thing you've noticed, out loud.

horse.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire and one of the four peach-blossom branches. The Horse loves openly and needs freedom badly, and it doesn't like hiding either one. That's why a situationship can make you restless and slightly furious: you'd rather run full speed or not at all. Use that. You're one of the people who can say what this is without much preamble. Just make sure the honesty runs both ways, including the part where you admit how much you'd like them to stay.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse spouse palace: full gallop or nothing. Situationships are a trot. You hate it.

goat.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Goat, 未, the warm late-summer Earth that stores Wood. The Goat is gentle, artistic and caring, and it worries in private. In close relationships you give comfort generously and assume that asking for it back would be too much. A situationship lets that imbalance hide, because nobody has agreed to look after anyone. Notice whether you're the one smoothing every rough patch. Then let them smooth one. Care that only flows one way isn't a relationship yet. It's a kindness.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat spouse palace: you comfort everyone. Let them comfort you once and watch.

monkey.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water in it, and one of the travel branches. The Monkey is quick, clever and allergic to boredom. You keep things lively and you're excellent at keeping them light, which is exactly how a situationship stays a situationship. When it gets serious, you crack a joke or change the subject. That's a reflex, not a choice. This time, let one serious moment stay serious. Count to five before you reach for the joke.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey spouse palace: you joke your way out of every real moment. Count to five.

rooster.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal and one of the four peach-blossom branches. The Rooster is polished, precise and honest, sometimes sharply so. Up close you notice flaws and you have standards, which protects you from settling and can also make you critique a person instead of asking for what you need. In an undefined setup you might be quietly grading them. Trade one critique for one request. Instead of they never plan anything, try I'd love it if you planned our next date.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster spouse palace: swap one critique for one request. Same point, kinder road.

dog.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth that stores Fire. The Dog is loyal, protective and principled, and it guards its heart until it's sure. You probably decided early whether this person is trustworthy, and you're loyal to that decision even when the evidence wobbles. A situationship confuses a Dog, because loyalty wants a clear person to be loyal to. Ask for the clarity your loyalty deserves. You're not being difficult. You're asking what you're guarding.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog spouse palace: loyal before they've earned it. Ask what you're guarding.

pig.text: In saju the branch under your Day Master, your day branch, is called the spouse palace. Yours is the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood in it, and one of the travel branches. The Pig is warm, generous, romantic and trusting. You see the best in people and give them time to grow into it. In a situationship that generosity can turn into waiting for potential, staying for who they could be rather than who they are this month. Keep the warmth. Add one question you'd ask a friend's date: what are they actually doing to show up for me?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig spouse palace: you love their potential. Check what they're doing this month.

base.why-you-stay: Gap Wood doesn't quit things. You see potential, you see a direction, and you'd rather build than walk away. In a situationship that instinct can keep you planting in soil that never agreed to be a garden. You tell yourself it's growing slowly, that they need time, that you'll know more next month. Sometimes that's true. Often you're staying because leaving would feel like admitting a project failed. Ask yourself plainly: am I here because this feels good now, or because I've already invested so much? Those are very different reasons, and only one of them is about joy.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You see so much potential in them, Gap. That's lovely.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Potential isn't a relationship. It's a pitch deck.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: It's okay to want something defined.

spring.intro: Spring Gap Wood wants to know where things are growing, and fast. Wood commanded your birth season, doubling your own element, so you like direction, labels and a plan you can stand behind. A situationship should drive you up the wall, and secretly it does. So why are you still in one? Often because you decided to be the patient one, the bigger tree, the person who doesn't need to ask. Pride dressed up as chill. The spring tree's honest move is the one it's best at: stand up straight and say what you want. You're not built for vague. You never were. Stop pretending the fog suits you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You, the most decisive tree alive, have been seeing where it goes since March?

summer.intro: A summer tree burns its energy outward, and Fire ruled the month you were born, Gap. Wood feeds Fire, so you express care loudly: plans, favors, enthusiasm, the effort of three people. In a situationship that means you're probably doing most of the work. You suggest the dates, keep the chat alive, show up with snacks. And because you're giving, it feels like a relationship to you, while it may feel like a nice warm hobby to them. Summer Gap's lesson is to notice the ratio. Stop fueling it for a week and watch what they put in. Their effort, not your fire, tells you what this is.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Try pausing the effort for a week. Let them show you their half.

autumn.intro: Autumn put Metal in charge of your birth season, Gap, and Metal is the axe to your tree. You grew up with rules and a quiet dread of being cut down. In a situationship that can make you careful in a way that doesn't look like you. You hold back the question because asking feels like handing someone the axe. So you wait, prune your own needs and call it being low-maintenance. Here's the autumn twist: Metal also shapes Wood into something useful. A clear boundary is your best tool, not your enemy. Decide your own terms first. Then a no from them is information, not a verdict.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Calling yourself low-maintenance while quietly starving is not a personality, Gap.

winter.intro: Winter Gap Wood lives on what's underground. Water ruled your season and Water nourishes Wood, so you can survive a long time on very little sunlight: a good text here, a memorable night there. That's exactly how a situationship keeps you. You're rooted enough to wait and patient enough to make it look fine. But being able to live on scraps isn't the same as being fed. The winter blind spot is mistaking endurance for contentment. Ask yourself what you'd want if spring arrived tomorrow. If the answer is more than this, you already know. Waiting quietly won't make them guess it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You can survive on crumbs, Gap. You deserve a whole meal.

earth.intro: The Earth days end every season, Gap, and you were born in them: a tall tree in heavy ground. Wood controls Earth, so you treat a situationship like terrain to manage. You map it, plan around it, and keep it moving forward in your head while saying very little out loud. The other person may think you're casual. You're actually building. The drift happens because your plans are silent. The talk for you is short and structural: what you want, what you're offering, and a clear question. Then let them answer without managing the reply.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've drawn up blueprints, Gap. They haven't seen a single page.

cliff.text: You probably know exactly what you want. You just haven't said it, because for Gap Wood saying it out loud means committing to the outcome.

sample.text: When signals are mixed, you tend to grab the most hopeful one and build a plan on top of it.

base.why-you-stay: Eul Wood is the vine, and vines wrap around whatever is nearby. In a situationship you adapt to their rhythm: when they text, when they're free, what they're ready for. You're so good at making things easy that you can stay a long time without noticing you're always the one adjusting. You stay because connection matters to you, and some connection feels better than none. That's human. But ask yourself one gentle question: do I feel more secure since this started, or less? Your honest answer tells you more than any of their texts ever could.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You make everything so easy for them, Eul.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Maybe too easy. When did they last adjust anything for you?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your want is allowed to be bigger than this.

spring.intro: Spring-born Eul Wood is a vine in a season full of trellises. Wood doubled up in your birth month, so you connect easily and adapt beautifully. That's precisely why situationships find you. You can make almost anything work: their vague texts, their weekend-only availability, their line about being bad at labels. You wind yourself around the shape they offer and make it look pretty. The spring blind spot is too many supports and no commitment from any of them. You might even be keeping two or three half-things alive. Ask which one you'd actually choose if you had to. Adaptable is a gift. Infinitely flexible is a trap.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've turned 'I'm bad at labels' into a cute garden feature. Stop decorating it.

summer.intro: In summer, Eul Wood blooms for an audience. Fire commanded your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so your charm pours out: playful messages, great photos, the effortless fun person. In a situationship you've likely become the highlight reel. Light, easy, never heavy. The problem is that a bloom that never asks for water eventually droops. You may be hiding how much you want more because wanting seems unattractive. It isn't. Summer Eul's honesty move is small: let them see one serious thing. A real question, a real feeling. How they handle a little weight tells you whether this can hold your full bloom.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to be the fun one every time. Show one real feeling.

autumn.intro: Autumn Eul grew up under Metal's shears. That season put the controlling element in charge of your birth month, which made you skilled at reading rules nobody says out loud. In a situationship you probably know their moods better than they do. You adjust your texts, your timing, your availability. You avoid the talk because you can already feel the scissors. But constant adjusting makes you smaller, and you can't negotiate a relationship you're too pruned to show up in. The autumn gift is resilience: you recover from cuts better than most. Which means you can afford to ask. Whatever the answer, you'll grow.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You rewrote one text eleven times to sound casual. That's not casual, Eul.

winter.intro: Winter Eul is a bulb waiting under the frost. Water ruled your season and feeds your Wood, so your inner world is rich and patient. In a situationship you can wait a long time for a sign: a hint, a 'we should', a hand held in public once. You live on what might bloom. The winter blind spot is that bulbs can stay underground for years if nobody turns up the heat. You might be waiting for them to make it warm enough to come out and ask. You can bring your own warmth. Say the small true thing. Let it be cold for a minute. Then see what grows.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to come up out of the frost and ask, Eul.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Eul, you're a vine finding cracks in packed soil. Wood controls Earth, so you're good at getting what you need sideways: a hint here, an easy invitation there, a mood that says more than words. In a situationship that works for a while. Then you realize you've arranged your whole week around someone who still hasn't said what this is. The signal you send is flexibility, and they read it as fine with anything. Say one direct thing. Vines can climb straight up when they choose to.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Being easy to be with doesn't mean you need nothing, Eul. Say what you need.

cliff.text: You might honestly not know what you want, because you've been tuned to what they want for a while.

sample.text: When signals are mixed, you bend to fit them.

base.why-you-stay: Byeong Fire is the sun, and you love the fun parts: the spark, the late calls, the inside jokes nobody else gets. A situationship can be all highlights and no responsibility, and honestly that's enjoyable for a while. You stay because when it's good, it's really good. But suns need warmth back too. If you've noticed you're giving more energy than you're getting, the fun can start to feel like a performance you're putting on twice a week. Ask yourself: if the fun nights stopped tomorrow, what would actually be left between you?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: When it's good, it's so good. I get it, Byeong.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And when it's not, you just shine harder. Exhausting.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Say what you want without the joke.

spring.intro: A spring sun rises with fuel to spare. Wood ruled your birth season and feeds your Fire, so you approach a situationship with optimism: it's fun, it's fine, it'll turn into something. You probably light up every hangout and make the in-between feel warmer than it is. That generosity is beautiful and slightly convenient for them. Why define anything when the sun shows up regardless? Spring Byeong's habit is assuming warmth will grow a relationship on its own. Warmth helps. Roots need commitment. Ask yourself whether they've done anything to earn the morning light, or whether you simply rise anyway.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd rise for them even if they never asked. They know that, Byeong.

summer.intro: A summer-born sun runs at full blaze. Fire ruled your season and doubled your element, so you're intense, generous and very visible. In a situationship that heat cuts both ways. You make it feel like the most exciting thing in their week, and then you get bored, run hot and cold, or blow it up with one dramatic message. Summer Byeong often keeps things undefined because a label feels like a smaller sky. Be honest: is the vagueness their choice or yours? If it's yours, own it out loud. If it's theirs, you deserve someone who wants to stand in your light on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Is it vague because of them, or because a label shrinks your sky?

autumn.intro: Autumn Byeong is a sun with work to do. Metal held the season you were born in, and Fire's role is to shape Metal, so you tend to treat love as something to build. In a situationship you might be trying to forge it into a relationship by sheer effort: being perfect company, solving their problems, proving you're worth choosing. It's admirable and exhausting. You can't hammer someone into commitment. The autumn sun's strength is clear, golden light. Use it to look honestly at what's there: what they offer, unprompted, week after week. That's the real shape of this. Decide from that shape, not from what you hope to make of it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Being perfect company every week isn't a job interview. Stop auditioning, Byeong.

winter.intro: A winter sun learns early that warmth can be taken away. Your birth season belonged to Water, Byeong, and Water is the element that dims Fire, so beneath all your brightness sits a worry about being too much and getting cooled down. In a situationship that worry becomes rules: don't double text, don't ask, don't show how much you care. You keep it light so nobody can douse you. But hiding your heat is still being doused, just by yourself. Winter Byeong's honest move is to let one ray through. Tell them you like them. If that cools them off, they were never going to warm your winter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your warmth isn't too much, Byeong. Let one honest ray through.

earth.intro: You arrived in the Earth days, Byeong, when the sun warms ground that keeps the heat for itself. Fire feeds Earth, so in a situationship you give generously: the plans, the energy, the good mood that makes every hangout feel like a date. They soak it up, and nothing much grows back. The drift comes when you notice you're always the one lighting things up. The talk for you is about reciprocity, said warmly: I like this, I'd like more back, what do you want? Ask it in daylight.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're running the whole sun for a 'haha same,' Byeong.

cliff.text: You know what you want, and you've probably already joked about it. Byeong Fire tends to say the true thing as a joke so it doesn't land too heavily.

sample.text: Instead of increasing your output, try matching theirs for a week.

base.why-you-stay: Jeong Fire is the candle, and when you connect, you connect deeply. Even an undefined thing feels intimate to you, because you bring your whole attention to it. You stay because the moments feel so real: the late talks, the small details they remember, the rare feeling of being understood. The question is whether that intimacy runs in both directions, or whether you're doing most of the feeling and quietly calling it us. Your depth is a gift. Make sure it's being received, not just enjoyed from a comfortable distance.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You bring so much depth to this, Jeong.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And they bring... a heart emoji every four days.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Wanting to feel special isn't needy.

spring.intro: A candle in spring has kindling everywhere. Wood ruled your birth season and feeds your Fire, so you have plenty of emotional fuel and you spend it on one person. In a situationship you probably think about them more than you'd admit, rereading messages, noticing every shift in tone. Every small spark feels like evidence. The spring blind spot is that a candle can burn brightly on its own fuel, which means you can feel a whole romance while they feel a nice thing. Check the kindling. How much of this fire is coming from them? You deserve someone who adds wood, not someone who only warms their hands.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've read meaning into a single heart emoji for three days. It's an emoji.

summer.intro: Summer Jeong burns with focused heat. Fire ruled your birth season and doubled your element, which makes you loyal, intense and selective about who gets close. Once you've chosen someone, a situationship doesn't feel casual to you at all. It feels like devotion without a title. You might be acting more committed than they are, then feeling quietly furious about it. Summer Jeong's habit is to keep burning and say nothing until the flame flares into a fight. Say it before then, calmly. Tell them you're exclusive in your head and ask where they are. Your intensity deserves clarity, not a slow burn on hope.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're already all in. It's fair to ask if they are too.

autumn.intro: Autumn Jeong is the careful flame that works on metal. Metal ruled your season, and Fire shapes Metal, so you love by attending to details and making things just right. In a situationship you've likely been quietly shaping it: the right timing, the right tone, the perfect moment to bring it up that never quite arrives. You're waiting for ideal conditions. They won't come. Autumn Jeong's trap is perfectionism disguised as patience. The talk doesn't need to be beautiful. It needs to happen. A plain question asked kindly will tell you more than a month of carefully crafted hints.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The perfect moment for the talk does not exist. Pick a Tuesday.

winter.intro: A winter candle guards itself against every draft. Your birth season belonged to Water, Jeong, and Water puts out Fire, so you learned to protect your feelings carefully. In a situationship that can mean you keep things undefined on purpose. If nothing is official, nothing can be lost. You give warmth in small, safe doses and tell yourself you don't mind the vagueness. Part of you does. Winter Jeong's honest question is whether this arrangement is protecting your flame or starving it. A candle in a sealed jar goes out too. Let a little air in. Ask for something you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keeping it undefined feels safer. Is it actually keeping you warm, Jeong?

earth.intro: The last weeks of a season are the Earth days, and you were born in them, Jeong. A candle in a clay room: your warmth stays close and makes the space feel safe. Fire feeds Earth, so in a situationship you create comfort, and comfort is easy to stay in without naming. You read every small signal, then keep your conclusions to yourself. The drift is two people getting cozy without deciding anything. The talk for you can be gentle and specific: one sentence about what you feel, one question about what they want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Cozy isn't the same as clear, Jeong. You're allowed to want both.

cliff.text: Being special to them is what you want, in a clear and steady way.

sample.text: Jeong Fire reads every detail and builds meaning from it.

base.why-you-stay: Mu Earth is the mountain: patient, steady, slow to move. In a situationship you wait. You assume things will settle into a shape if you just keep being reliable. At first you may not even mind the low pressure, since it asks nothing dramatic of you. You stay because leaving would require a decision you haven't fully made, and because you're loyal even to things without a name. Ask yourself one practical question: am I waiting for something specific to happen, or am I just waiting because waiting is what I do?

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You've been so patient and steady, Mu.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Patient, or just not deciding? Be honest.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Wanting stability is reasonable.

spring.intro: Spring roots push through the mountain, and Wood commanded your birth season, Mu. Wood controls Earth, which gave you patience under pressure and a habit of letting other people's needs grow through you. In a situationship you've probably become wonderfully accommodating. Their schedule, their pace, their uncertainty. You don't complain, you hold steady. And it works, for them. Spring Mu's blind spot is forgetting that a mountain is allowed to have terms. You're not difficult for wanting to know what this is. Name one thing you need, a plan, a label, a weekend, and see whether they make room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Being endlessly accommodating isn't a love language, Mu. It's a rental agreement.

summer.intro: A summer mountain is solid and sun-warmed. Your season belonged to Fire, Mu, and Fire generates Earth, so you have a steady confidence most people envy. In a situationship that makes you look unbothered. You're happy to keep showing up, reliable as ever. But steady can also mean stuck. You might stay in this simply because leaving would require movement, and mountains don't love moving. Summer Mu's honest question isn't whether they'll commit. It's whether you're still here by choice or by inertia. You can feel secure and still want more. Wanting more is not instability.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Feeling secure and wanting more can both be true, Mu.

autumn.intro: Autumn Mu gives freely, the way a mountain gives up ore. Your birth season belonged to Metal and Earth produces Metal, so you show care through practical help: driving them places, fixing their laptop, being the dependable one. In a situationship you've likely become indispensable without becoming official. They lean on you. They don't label you. The autumn blind spot is believing usefulness will eventually be rewarded with commitment. Sometimes it is. Often it just gets used. Watch what happens when you stop solving things for a while. A partner shows up for you too. A situationship mostly shows up when it needs something.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You fixed their laptop, moved their sofa, still no label. Interesting pattern, Mu.

winter.intro: Winter Mu is the dam holding back a frozen river. Water was in command when you were born, and Earth controls Water, so you're excellent at containing feelings: yours, theirs, everyone's. In a situationship that means you keep it calm. No drama, no demands, no messy questions. You manage the emotional temperature so well that nobody, including you, notices how much you want. The winter blind spot is control that slowly becomes silence. Let one feeling out without managing it first. Tell them you'd like more. The river won't flood the valley. It'll just show both of you what's actually been building.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your feelings aren't a flood risk, Mu. Let one out and see.

earth.intro: Earth days are your own season, Mu, so you were born with extra mountain in you. In a situationship you're steady, patient and slow to make a move, which can look like indifference from the outside. You might be waiting for proof before you say anything, and they might be waiting for a sign from you. Two people waiting is how situationships last a year. The talk for you doesn't need a speech. Say the solid thing once: I'm interested in more. Mountains don't have to move far to change the view.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Patience is great, Mu. Patience with zero words is a mystery novel.

cliff.text: You want stability, someone you can actually count on. Mu Earth rarely says that out loud, because you'd rather show it than ask for it.

sample.text: Give you a mixed signal and you tend to ignore them and hold your course.

base.why-you-stay: Gi Earth is the garden, and you nurture whatever is in front of you. In a situationship you probably give a lot: you listen, you help, you remember things, you make every evening cozy. You stay because caring is your way of loving, and because part of you hopes that enough care will eventually turn this into something real. Ask yourself, gently but honestly: is this growing because of us, or only because of me? If you stopped watering it for two weeks, would anything still be standing? That question can sting a little. Answer it anyway, quietly, just for yourself.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You make everything so warm for them, Gi.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Unpaid caretaking for someone who won't commit. Love that for you.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You're allowed to want care back.

spring.intro: Spring soil feeds whatever's planted in it. Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gi, and Wood controls Earth, so you instinctively make space for other people to grow. In a situationship you've probably been nourishing them generously: listening to their stress, backing their plans, being the soft landing. They grow. You wait. Spring Gi tends to think that if you tend well enough, commitment will sprout on its own. Sometimes the seed just isn't the kind that roots. Look at what you get back. Are they tending you at all? Good soil deserves a gardener too, not just a tenant.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're their emotional support garden. Unpaid. No lease. Think about that, Gi.

summer.intro: Summer Gi is warm, fertile and full of care. Your season belonged to Fire and Fire feeds Earth, so you're well supported inside and generous on the outside. In a situationship you probably create comfort without trying: the cozy nights in, the little care packages, the way you remember things. The risk for warm Gi is building a relationship's whole atmosphere without its commitment. They get the home feeling without the home. Summer Gi's question is simple. If you stopped hosting, what would they bring to the table? You're not asking too much by wanting a guest who becomes a partner.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You make everything cozy. You deserve someone who brings the blanket too.

autumn.intro: Autumn is harvest, and Gi Earth is the thing being harvested. Your birth season belonged to Metal and Earth gives rise to Metal, so you pour yourself into results: helpful, competent, always delivering. In a situationship you might be over-performing to stay valuable. Never needy, always easy, always useful. Autumn Gi's blind spot is believing affection has to be earned with output. It doesn't. Notice how much of this connection depends on you giving and them receiving. Try being slightly less useful for two weeks. What remains when you stop producing is what's really between you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Try being less helpful for two weeks. Terrifying, I know. Do it anyway.

winter.intro: Winter Gi is soil holding cold water: absorbent, quiet, carrying more than it shows. Water was in command when you were born, and Earth controls Water, so you're always shaping feelings into something manageable. In a situationship you probably absorb the ambiguity for both of you. Their mixed signals soak into you and you turn them into reasons to stay. Winter Gi can go muddy: everything blurred, no clear edges. What you need is a firm line, even a small one. Decide what would make you feel secure, say a weekly plan or a real label, and say it plainly. Clear edges make soil fertile, not soggy.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A small, clear line is kind to both of you, Gi.

earth.intro: Born in the Earth days, Gi, your own element runs strong. You're the garden: you notice what someone needs and quietly provide it. In a situationship that turns into doing relationship things without a relationship: the snacks, the check-ins, the remembering. They get the benefits of partnership, and you get the uncertainty. The drift is you tending something they haven't committed to tend back. The talk for you is about fairness, said kindly. What are we building, and are we both building it?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You've been tending this garden alone, Gi. Ask who else holds a shovel.

cliff.text: You want to be taken care of too. Gi Earth often forgets to put that on the list at all.

sample.text: Faced with mixed signals, you worry, and then you try harder.

base.why-you-stay: Gyeong Metal is the blade, direct and loyal. Honestly, situationships aren't your natural habitat, because you like things clear and labeled. So if you're in one, something about this person got past your defences. You might be staying out of pride, not wanting to be the one who cares more first. Or you said casual at the beginning, and you keep your word even when it no longer fits. Check whether that early promise still matches who you are now, or whether you're just being loyal to an old sentence.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You care about honesty more than anything, Gyeong.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Then why are you in a situationship? That's your opposite.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Asking where you stand isn't weakness.

spring.intro: A spring axe faces a whole forest, and Your birth season belonged to Wood, Gyeong. Metal cuts Wood, so you're wired to act, decide and conquer what's in front of you. In a situationship the ambiguity is almost physically uncomfortable. You might have asked about it already, bluntly, and been told it's complicated. Or you might be treating them like a project to win. Spring Gyeong's blind spot is chasing: too many trees, all hacked at once. Instead of pushing for an answer, state your position once, clearly, and stop. Your directness is a gift when you say it and then let them choose.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: State it once, Gyeong. Then stop swinging. Chasing isn't the same as clarity.

summer.intro: Summer-born metal was made in the forge. Fire was in command when you were born, Gyeong, and Fire melts Metal, so you're used to pressure and good at enduring heat. In a situationship you may be enduring too well. You tell yourself it's fine, you're tough, you don't need labels. Meanwhile the vagueness is quietly melting your patience. Summer Gyeong's risk is the sudden snap: weeks of silence, then one cold message that ends it. Before you get there, let the heat out in a measured way. Tell them what you want while you're still calm. A sword is strongest tempered, not overheated.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say it while you're calm, Gyeong. Not after the snap.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gyeong is metal at its most absolute. Metal was in command when you were born and doubled your element, so you value loyalty, straight answers and clear lines. A situationship is the opposite of everything you trust. So why are you in one? Maybe because you're testing them silently, waiting to see if they're worthy before you commit. Gyeong can hold out, waiting for proof before giving any, while they wait for the same from you. Two swords crossed, nobody moving. Lower yours slightly. Show your loyalty first. Then their response is the honest answer you've been waiting for.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two people waiting to see who blinks first. Romance of the century, Gyeong.

winter.intro: Winter Gyeong is steel near a cold river. You were born while Water was in charge and Metal generates Water, so your strength flows out as thinking. In a situationship you probably analyze everything privately: what they meant, what they want, how it might go. You keep your face neutral and your feelings locked. They may genuinely not know you care. Winter Gyeong's blind spot is assuming your loyalty is obvious when you've never actually said it. Let the water carry a message. Say I like you, plainly. You're braver than almost anyone. Spend some of that courage on the soft words.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They might not know you care, Gyeong. Tell them in plain words.

earth.intro: The Earth days feed Metal, and you were born in them, Gyeong: ore with plenty of mountain behind it. You feel secure in yourself, which makes you seem unbothered in a situationship. You won't chase. You also won't soften, so the other person may not know you care. The drift is mutual pride: neither of you wants to be the one who asks. The talk for you should be plain and short, which suits you. Here's what I want. What do you want? No debate, no scoring.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Not chasing is fine, Gyeong. Not saying anything at all is just stubborn.

cliff.text: You want clarity and loyalty, plainly. Gyeong Metal knows this about itself. You might have avoided saying it because asking feels like showing weakness, like handing over a point.

sample.text: Mixed signals frustrate you more than most people.

base.why-you-stay: Sin Metal is the jewel, refined and selective. You don't fall easily, so if you're in a situationship, this person impressed you. You might stay because you like the idea of them, or because asking for more feels like exposing yourself in an unflattering light. You'd rather be elegantly casual than visibly invested. Ask yourself honestly: is the casualness real, or is it a very beautiful cover for wanting something you're scared to ask for? Only you know, and you probably already do. Write the answer in one honest line, just for yourself. Nobody else needs to see it.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You don't fall easily, Sin. They must have impressed you.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: And now you're pretending to be casual. Elegantly. Badly.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Your standards are not too high.

spring.intro: A spring jewel sits in a garden of options. Wood was in command when you were born, Sin, and Metal shapes Wood, so you have a refined eye and plenty of choice. In a situationship that can make you the hesitant one. You like them, but you're not sure they're quite right, and committing feels like closing the display case for good. Spring Sin keeps things open while quietly judging. Be honest about whose vagueness this is. If it's yours, they deserve to know. If it's theirs, your standards apply here too. You'd never accept half-effort in anything else you love.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your standards are sky high for shoes and nonexistent for texting back. Curious, Sin.

summer.intro: Summer Sin was polished in the heat. Fire was in command when you were born, and Fire tests Metal, so you're sensitive to criticism and very good at seeming fine. In a situationship that sensitivity turns every delayed reply into a verdict on you. You might not ask what this is because rejection would scratch too deep. So you stay perfect and agreeable and wait to be chosen. Summer Sin's lesson is that heat reveals what's real. Asking a clear question is heat. It's uncomfortable, but it shows you whether this is gold or plating. Either answer protects your shine in the long run.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A slow reply isn't a verdict on you, Sin. It's just a slow reply.

autumn.intro: Autumn Sin is the jewel at full sparkle. Metal ruled your birth month and doubled your element, which gives you strong standards, strong pride and a clear sense of what you deserve. In a situationship, pride can stop you admitting you want more. You play it cool and elegant, as if you could take or leave them. They might believe you. Sin's blind spot here is waiting to be chosen instead of choosing. You don't lose value by saying you'd like this to be real. You gain clarity. Say it in your own polished way, then let their answer show you their worth.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Playing it so cool they think you don't care. Great acting, Sin. Terrible strategy.

winter.intro: Winter Sin sparkles under ice. You were born while Water was in charge and Metal generates Water, so you're perceptive, articulate and often three steps ahead in reading the situation. You've probably already worked out what this is. You just don't like the answer. In a situationship winter Sin tends to narrate rather than act: brilliant voice notes to friends, sharp analysis, no actual conversation with the person involved. Your insight is real. It's wasted if it only goes to the group chat. Take one of those perfect sentences you've said about them and say it to them instead.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your group chat already heard the speech. Maybe they should hear it too.

earth.intro: You were born in the Earth days, Sin, a jewel in rich soil. Earth feeds you, but too much of it can cover your shine. In a situationship you hold high standards and say almost none of them out loud, waiting to see if they'll notice on their own. They usually don't. Meanwhile you keep it polished and pleasant on the surface. The drift happens in that silence. The talk for you means letting a standard be seen: I want consistency. I want to know where I stand.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your standards aren't too high, Sin. They're just hidden. Show one.

cliff.text: You want to be treasured. Seen in detail. Chosen with intention, not by default.

sample.text: Faced with mixed signals, you analyze them with precision and then pretend you didn't notice anything.

base.why-you-stay: Im Water is the ocean, and you love your freedom. Honestly, a situationship can suit you for a while. No pressure, plenty of space, nobody asking where you are on a Saturday. You might stay because it's easy, or because defining it would feel like signing up for a cage. But check yourself here. Are you genuinely happy with how undefined it is, or are you avoiding the question because answering it would mean staying in one harbor for longer than you're used to? Both answers are allowed. Just make sure it's the real one.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You love your freedom, Im. That's real.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: You also love not answering hard questions. Also real.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Maybe you want freedom with someone.

spring.intro: Spring Im is a river feeding everything along its banks. Wood was in command when you were born and Water nourishes Wood, so you give energy freely: ideas, adventures, encouragement. In a situationship you probably make it exciting. Spontaneous trips, late calls, big plans for later. You might also be the one keeping it undefined, because freedom feels like oxygen. Spring Im's question is whether the vagueness serves you or just keeps options open out of habit. If you want it to grow, flowing in every direction won't do it. Pick a channel. Even rivers choose a path to the sea.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You love freedom so much a situationship became your whole lifestyle, Im.

summer.intro: Summer Im runs warm and restless. You were born while Fire was in charge, and Water controls Fire, so you're used to managing heat: excitement, chaos, other people's moods. In a situationship you might be the one keeping everything breezy. You cool down any intensity, change the subject when it gets serious, keep the fun going. It works until you notice you're managing them instead of being with them. Summer Im's honest move is to stop steering for a moment. Let a serious conversation happen without rescuing it with a joke. See what they say when the water is still.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to cool every serious moment with a joke, Im.

autumn.intro: Autumn Im springs clear and cold from stone. Metal was in command when you were born and generates Water, so your chart is strong: confident, deep, self-sufficient. In a situationship that self-sufficiency can be the issue. You don't need them, so you never ask. You enjoy the connection, then vanish into your own plans for a week. They might read that as low interest. Strong autumn Im's blind spot is assuming everyone can handle your tides. If you want this to be something, show up consistently for a while. If you don't, say so kindly. Either is fairer than drifting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Vanishing for a week then sending a meme is not a communication strategy, Im.

winter.intro: Winter Im is the deep sea at its fullest. Water held your season and doubled your element, so you feel enormously and show very little. In a situationship you might be secretly invested and outwardly breezy, a calm surface hiding strong currents. You can keep this up for months. The winter blind spot is that nobody can navigate water they can't see. They may be guessing, just like you. Winter Im needs a shoreline: a clear moment where you say what you feel and ask what they want. It doesn't have to be dramatic. Just real enough to break the surface.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They can't read currents they can't see, Im. Show a little.

earth.intro: Im, you met walls early: you were born in the Earth days. Earth controls Water, so you're used to pushing against limits and flowing around them. A situationship can feel perfect at first because there are no banks at all. Then the lack of shape starts to bother you, and you drift off to see if anyone follows. That's a test the other person doesn't know they're taking. The talk for you is about structure, not feelings first: how often, how serious, how exclusive. Banks make rivers go somewhere.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Disappearing to see if they notice is a quiz they never signed up for, Im.

cliff.text: You might want something deeper than you're admitting. Im Water often thinks it wants freedom, when what it really wants is freedom with someone.

sample.text: Im Water flows, warm and present one week, distant and busy the next, and doesn't always notice the change from the outside.

base.why-you-stay: Gye Water is the rain, intuitive and gentle. You feel deeply and quietly, and a situationship lets you keep those feelings unspoken, which can feel safe. You might stay because you sense something real between you, a connection that doesn't need words. Or because asking would feel far too exposing. Ask yourself softly: is the mystery here romantic, or is it just unclear? Romantic mystery makes you feel more alive. Unclear makes you feel more anxious. You can tell the difference if you're honest. Put your hand on your chest, ask the question, and notice what comes up first.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: You feel so much, Gye, even when you don't say it.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Exactly. You don't say it. They're not mind readers.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: Writing your feelings down first is a great idea.

spring.intro: Spring Gye is soft rain that helps things grow. You were born while Wood was in charge and Water feeds Wood, so your care is quiet, attentive and generous. In a situationship you're probably the one who listens, remembers and checks in. Your attention helps them bloom, and you hope it'll make them notice what's right in front of them. Spring Gye's trap is giving softly and waiting to be seen. They might not see it, not because you aren't worth it but because rain is easy to take for granted. Say what you want in words. Hints are lovely. Words are clear.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hints are lovely. They have also not worked for four months, Gye.

summer.intro: A summer cloud has a lot of heat to cool. You were born while Fire was in charge, Gye, and Water controls Fire, so you're constantly soothing, smoothing, keeping things pleasant. In a situationship you might be absorbing all the heat: their unpredictability, their busy weeks, their vague plans. You make it easy for them and hard for yourself. Summer Gye can evaporate, slowly losing yourself in their weather. Notice whether you feel more yourself or less since this started. If less, it's time to ask for something solid. A plan. A label. A sign they're bringing some shade too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Do you feel more like yourself since this started, or less? Be honest, Gye.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gye is mist rising off cold stone, well fed by Metal, which ruled your birth season. Metal generates Water, so your intuition is sharp and usually right. You already sense what this situationship is and isn't. The issue isn't reading the signals. It's trusting them. Autumn Gye can second-guess a clear read because the hopeful version is so vivid. Write down what you actually feel about where this is heading, then compare it with what they've actually done. Your gut has been taking notes. Let it speak when you have the talk.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut figured this out weeks ago. Your hope is filibustering, Gye.

winter.intro: Winter Gye is snow, quiet and complete. Water held your season and doubled your element, so your imagination runs rich and your feelings run deep. In a situationship you can build an entire relationship in your head: future trips, inside jokes, how you'd introduce them. The real one is thinner. Winter Gye's blind spot is preferring the imagined version because it never disappoints. But it also never holds you. Bring one daydream into the real world. Suggest one of those plans. Their response, in actual life, is the clarity you've been looking for.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Take one daydream and actually suggest it, Gye. Real life is warmer.

earth.intro: Gye, you arrived at the tail of a season, in the Earth days: rain falling on dry ground. Earth controls Water, so what you feel often sinks in without a trace. In a situationship you pick up every shift in tone, then quietly decide not to mention it. They may have no idea how much you're reading. The drift is your silence plus their vagueness. The talk for you starts small: one observation, one feeling, one question. You don't need the full forecast. Just let them feel a drop.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You've noticed everything, Gye. Tell them one thing you noticed.

cliff.text: You want emotional closeness, to be understood without having to explain every single thing.

sample.text: When the messages don't add up, you absorb them.
